claims.text: Adding silicon to phosphorus-containing high-entropy or compositionally complex alloys improves glass-forming ability.
Adding silicon to phosphorus-containing high-entropy or compositionally complex alloys improves the thermal stability of the amorphous state.
The proposed intervention is the addition of silicon.
Silicon addition may modify atomic structure and bonding in the alloy.
Changes in atomic structure and bonding may influence glass-forming ability.
Changes in atomic structure and bonding may influence the thermal stability of the amorphous state.
The proposed improvement may depend on alloy composition, cooling rate, and processing conditions.
The expected improvements are relative to otherwise comparable phosphorus-containing alloys without silicon addition.
The effect is expected to be limited to particular alloy compositions and processing conditions.
The amount of silicon required, the responsive alloy compositions, and the underlying mechanism are uncertain.
The hypothesis can be tested by systematically varying silicon content and measuring glass-forming ability, thermal stability, and microstructure.
Failure of silicon addition to improve both glass-forming ability and thermal stability across multiple compositions and processing conditions would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis refers to addition of a specific amount of silicon, but no amount is specified and the uncertainty field states that the required amount is unknown.
